However, this legal campaign was launched without the prior direct notification of the site administrators, a procedural omission that bypasses standard communication channels.", "summary": "The MPAA publicly sued seven file-sharing sites without first notifying their administrators."}, "1": {"original": "The MPAA publicly sued BitTorrent and Usenet sites without notifying them first,", "rephrased": "The Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA) publicly initiated legal action against BitTorrent and Usenet sites without first notifying the site administrators, a procedural failure that has caused significant distress to the operators. This approach contrasts sharply with standard legal practices where affected parties are given the opportunity to resolve issues privately before public litigation ensues.", "summary": "The MPAA publicly sued file-sharing sites without first notifying the administrators."}, "2": {"original": "Administrators would have appreciated prior notification before the lawsuits", "rephrased": "The administrators of the targeted file-sharing websites expressed that they would have greatly appreciated receiving direct notification from the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA) before the lawsuits were announced to the public. They argue that a private, initial contact would have allowed them to address the concerns internally and resolve the matter without the reputational damage caused by a public legal battle.", "summary": "File-sharing site administrators would have preferred prior private notification before public lawsuits."}, "3": {"original": "We would have cooperated with the MPAA if contacted personally, but being", "rephrased": "The administrators of the dvdrs.net website stated that they would have been willing to cooperate fully with the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA) had they been contacted personally regarding copyright concerns. They emphasize that being publicly sued without prior notice is an outrage, arguing that their site operates within international laws and that the public announcement has unfairly destroyed the reputation they have built over two years.", "summary": "The dvdrs.net administrators would have cooperated with the MPAA if contacted privately."}}
